bug_semantics: load_time_series_segmentation_benchmark parses TSSB CSV columns change_points and time_series with pandas converters that call Python eval() on each cell, then wrap the result in np.array. A user-supplied or attacker-hosted CSV/zip (local extract_path or the downloaded tssb.csv) can therefore inject and execute arbitrary Python in the loader process (CWE-94). The same eval converter pattern existed in load_human_activity_segmentation_datasets in the same file. The security fix replaced eval with ast.literal_eval inside _parse_np_array.
flaw_origin: The eval() CSV converters were first written when the TSSB/HAS data loaders were added in PR #1755. The reconstructable first-write member 849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f created aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py with converters = {col: lambda val: np.array(eval(val)) for col in np_cols} in load_time_series_segmentation_benchmark (and a sibling eval converter in load_human_activity_segmentation_datasets). The file and eval sink are absent from that commit parent 800c3b5388219850c853d14201a9e841187851f6. GitHub squash-merged the PR as 8f81a7324a4f116dd862feda68788b03ff9dc39b onto main; later typing/typo commits did not change the eval mechanism.
